comparison: Perfect agreement on intact rat cortical stimulation effects (C15-C23). Both evaluations find these baseline findings well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and dose-response relationships, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these as foundational data for post-injury comparisons.

Substantial overlap on post-SCI ipsilesional stimulation effects (C26-C36). Both find evidence supported, though they group claims differently. OpenEval includes all bilateral synergy claims (C24-C39) while peer review R1 focuses on specific kinematic and EMG effects (C26-C36, C42-C44) plus ablation controls (C66-C67). Both affirm the robustness of these findings.

Partial overlap on longitudinal stimulation effects (C29, C37-C39). OpenEval groups these with immediate bilateral synergy effects in a comprehensive evaluation, while peer review R8 treats them as technical validation of persistent effects. Both find the evidence supported.

Overlap on EMG evidence (C42-C44). OpenEval evaluates these as mechanistic support for kinematic findings, while peer review R1 includes them as part of the broader demonstration of ipsilesional cortex effects. Both find evidence supported.

Partial overlap on injury characterization (C40-C41). OpenEval groups EMG findings separately from injury baseline, while peer review R6 treats injury deficits as contextual observations. Both find evidence supported.

Overlap on postural effects (C45-C46). OpenEval emphasizes both immediate neuroprosthetic and spontaneous recovery aspects, while peer review R6 treats these as injury characterization. Both find evidence supported.
Minimal overlap on posture (C47). OpenEval includes this in comprehensive posture evaluation, peer review R1 includes it among solidly demonstrated effects. Both find evidence supported.

Strong overlap on motor mapping findings (C48-C54). Both evaluations find the longitudinal mapping data and corticospinal transmission changes well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and within-subject correlations, peer reviewers praise the careful examination of motor map recovery.

Overlap on correlation analyses (C55-C59). OpenEval includes these in comprehensive motor mapping evaluation, peer review R4 treats them as part of careful correlation analysis. Both find the nuanced pattern of within-subject but not across-subject correlations well-supported.

Strong agreement on ipsilateral flexion effects (C60-C65) but different evaluation outcomes. OpenEval finds evidence supported despite N=2, emphasizing statistical significance and spatial consistency. Peer review R2 rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample size and lack of ablation control for this specific effect, identifying it as a weakness.

Overlap on anatomical determinants (C83-C86). OpenEval finds the negative correlation findings appropriately acknowledged as limiting mechanistic interpretation. Peer review R10 rates as UNCERTAIN, citing concerns about small N=2 sample and limited data for negative findings.

Agreement on ablation controls (C66-C67). Both find evidence that ipsilateral cortical effects persist without contralateral cortex well-supported. OpenEval notes consistency across all three ablation subjects, peer reviewers explicitly confirm ablation does not impede reported effects.

Perfect agreement on long-train stimulation effects (C68-C72, C87-C89). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes bilateral spinal circuit activation and injury severity effects, peer reviewers treat these as valid observations supporting bilateral synergy interpretation.

Overlap on mechanistic interpretations (C73-C74, C90-C91) but different evaluation outcomes. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C74 is explicitly speculative and lacks direct experimental support. Peer review R9 rates as SUPPORTED, treating interpretations as reasonable conclusions that contribute to understanding of bilateral spinal circuitry.

Partial overlap on mechanistic synthesis (C81-C82). OpenEval finds these interpretations appropriately qualified and reasonable given supporting data. Peer review R9 affirms these contribute to understanding of bilateral spinal circuitry influence. Both find evidence supported.

Overlap on map size correlations (C78-C79). OpenEval includes these in synthesis about ipsilesional motor maps and recovery relationships. Peer review R3 treats them as part of careful motor mapping examination. Both find evidence supported.

Minimal overlap on cross-sectional correlations (C80). OpenEval includes this in comprehensive synthesis of map-recovery relationships. Peer review R4 treats it as part of nuanced correlation analysis. Both find evidence supported.

Strong agreement on background literature claims (C1-C2, C7-C12). Both evaluations find these appropriately characterized as established knowledge. OpenEval emphasizes they provide appropriate motivation, peer reviewers request clarity of terminology but do not dispute validity of cited evidence.

OpenEval evaluates temporal plasticity context claims (C75-C77) as supported, connecting observed patterns to established principles. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about temporal correlations and cortical plasticity literature.

OpenEval evaluates experimental design and power analysis claims (C92-C94) as supported, noting sound experimental design. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.

Peer review R2 rates ipsilateral flexion effects (C4, C60-C65) as UNCERTAIN due to N=2 and lack of ablation control. OpenEval addresses C60-C65 in R6 (rated SUPPORTED) but does not evaluate C4 separately.
